minutes.headline: Committee votes to recommend against acquiring 35 Lemonster Road; begins push for a town conservation fund
minutes.summary: The Open Space Committee, now an official standing committee under the town bylaw, heard a proposal from the town planning director to seek a small recurring annual town meeting appropriation for a conservation fund, modeled on a neighboring town's practice, to build capacity for future land purchases and grant matches. The committee voted to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on a 35 Lemonster Road parcel after reviewing it against acquisition criteria, and discussed revising those criteria and pursuing agricultural preservation restrictions on several parcels considered at risk of development.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on the 35 Lemonster Road parcel.
The planning director proposed asking future town meetings for a small recurring appropriation to build a dedicated conservation fund.
Members agreed to first consult the treasurer/collector and town manager on the steps to set up such a fund, targeting the fall town meeting to create it and the following annual meeting to fund it.
The committee began revising its land-acquisition criteria and flagged an agricultural preservation restriction for the Stillman family land as a priority to pursue.

why_it_matters: The Select Board acts next on 35 Lemonster Road; this recommendation is what it will weigh in deciding whether the town exercises its right of first refusal on the parcel.
A conservation fund, if established, would appear as a recurring line at town meeting -- potentially drawing on free cash -- that residents vote on each year rather than a one-time purchase.
Revised acquisition criteria and any agricultural preservation restrictions would shape which private parcels the town moves to protect from development going forward.
